key_insight: In the FAIR-ICI real-world cohort, survival extended beyond active immunotherapy for some patients, while outcomes were frequently less favorable than in pivotal trials.
clinical_relevance: Performance status was strongly associated with survival, highlighting the importance of patient characteristics when interpreting trial results in routine cancer care.
method: Retrospective cohort of 3,231 adults receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors at four Belgian hospitals.
Harmonized electronic health records using OMOP-CDM and natural language processing.
Evaluated treatment trajectories and survival, with descriptive trial comparisons and multivariable Cox regression.
evidence_signal: Among 568 metastatic patients who discontinued immunotherapy without subsequent systemic therapy, median post-discontinuation survival was 21.4 months; ECOG ≥2 was associated with poorer overall survival than ECOG 0–1 (adjusted HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.82–2.60).
watch_item: This observational treatment-outcomes study—not an AI drug-discovery study—cannot establish that discontinuation causes prolonged survival, and trial comparisons were descriptive.
paper_title: Comprehensive real-world utilization, treatment trajectories, and outcomes of immune checkpoint inhibitors across cancer types: the multicenter FAIR-ICI cohort
